title: Document requirement about metadata tables in Iceberg JDBC catalog
body:
# Context
Since **Trino release 414**, while using **Iceberg** with **JDBC catalog**, the tables for the catalog are not automatically created anymore. 

[This PR](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/pull/16557/files#diff-679b7ac4be81848b9b33211a518a7fa14d2666f71a2810a41b94f2aec6a4f292R94) introduced a change in behavior since previous versions (<= 413), where before these tables were automatically created. [^1]


# Motivation
Certain use-cases and scenarios could leverage the automated creation of Iceberg JDBC catalog tables (e.g. local development, fresh deployments, etc.). At this point in time the user is forced to create these tables manually.

# Solution
Expose the Iceberg property `initialize-catalog-tables` as a Trino catalog property: `iceberg.jdbc-catalog.initialize-catalog-tables`. This way users could control this behavior.

Note: I assume this is a _catalog property_, so it would not fit under the `extra_properties` _table property_.



[^1]: Note to the maintainers:
The above mentioned PR didn't include any release notes while it was upgrading the underlying catalog dependency (iceberg), which potentially can introduce difference in behavior. I believe such changes should always be mentioned in release notes, for better understanding of the differences in between versions, and to support easier back-tracing of regressions. 
While these type of changes are not necessarily or directly visible to the end users, they occasionally or indirectly can be.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> these tables were automatically created.

This is unexpected behavior. I wouldn't agree with the PR which supports initializing the tables. 

Why do you need to initialize those tables more than once? I suppose your metadata tables were created in old versions.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 Thanks for getting back on this. As mentioned in the description, there are 2 quite common scenarios that come to my mind:
- local development setups
- fresh deployments (1st time deployments like deployments to  new environments)

It's not about initializing more than once, it's about being able to initialize _at all_ (for times when it was not previously initialized), which you cannot just manually by hand since Trino version 414.

Also the underlying Iceberg functionality would create these when `enabled` only if they don't exist. 

I believe this is an expected behavior by the Iceberg maintainers as well as it's an existing functionality in Iceberg, but is currently hardcoded to `false` in Trino.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> If we expose the config and users try to enable it in the unsupported databases, **_we_** (not Iceberg community) will receive the blame.

While I don't see the reasoning behind your concern of users misusing the proposed functionality (especially with other catalogs / databases which are not scope of this change), I do appreciate your concern on Trino getting the blame instead of underlying dependencies.

From that blame angle, actually the current state (since Trino 414) would potentially cause what you are worried about in that aspect. Let's take the following example:
- A new user wants to use Trino, especially with Iceberg using the JDBC catalog
- The user downloads Trino and configures the Iceberg JDBC catalog appropriately against its RDBMS based on the Trino documentation
- User tries to use Trino with Iceberg JDBC catalog, but Trino fails with the following error, as the catalog tables are _not_ created: 
    ``` ```
- User tries to find something about this in Trino documentation / release notes, but as nothing related is found there, therefor "blames" Trino.

To avoid such situations, I'd imagine having the current state appropriately documented would be due as the minimum. In addition to the documentation bit, the proposed functionality this issue is about would help new users evaluate Trino (with Iceberg) in a easier and quicker fashion. (sparing the pain of the user finding the Iceberg catalog table DDLs and automate the creation of those tables separately)

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
JDBC catalog has other issues as well, most notably no way to manage schema upgrades on Iceberg version upgrade. In current shape of the JDBC catalog support in Iceberg I don't agree that making it easier to get started with Iceberg JDBC catalog should be a goal.

The fact that the auto-create functionality existed and was removed doesn't meant that the original situation with auto-create was the desired one.

Instead of saying "auto-create JDBC catalog tables" can you state what you would like to accomplish in more functional terms? Would having a procedure to initialize the Iceberg JDBC catalog solve your use-case? It's something the user will need to explicitly invoke and hence be better positioned to handle any issues arising from using Iceberg's `JdbcUtil`. Each additional config toggle we add adds burden on users to learn what they do and also increases the scenarios to be tested - it's a cost.

Or just adding documentation and updating release notes solve your use-case?

Regarding documentation, this being an existing functionality as part of the last couple of releases, updating documentation to reflect the current behavior would surely help existing and potential new users. This applies to Release notes as well.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hello, dear maintainers. I agree with the statement that Trino team could not be responsible for anything regarding things that breaks Trino in any point of view. But this issue here is much more than that: the Iceberg connector is LIMITING Iceberg features by not exposing this configuration for this connector only.

The proposed configuration is related to a feature that Iceberg's JDBC has. It is not something that would be transferring responsability to Trino. You may see here that this is an Iceberg feature: https://github.com/apache/iceberg/blob/319a482aadd96559bfe65ae103e1f7101f46bfe6/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/jdbc/JdbcCatalog.java#L100.

I'm an example of new user that just could not find a way to setup Trino + Iceberg + Postgres (as JDBC metadata store). I just could figure out yet how to do it, just because Trino don't let me to configure this Iceberg property. Really cannot understand the point on why the proposed PR was refused. And, respectfully, it seems that is just a misunderstanding from Trino team about this feature from Iceberg.

Why I, as user, should know in advance what kind of tables Iceberg would use to store it's metadata? It is not an user concern. Iceberg could even (in a new version, for instance) change something in this tables, that would be put in Iceberg JDBC driver the code to update it or recreate it and then, because of the Trino limitation on this flag, everything could broke. Metadata tables are responsability of Iceberg and that is the main point on why the PR should be accepted. Till then, I, as user, blame Trino to block me on this. So I really do not think that the solution for this is putting on the docs how I create by myself this tables in Postgres. Does not make any sense.

Btw, congratulations for the work in Trino. Even not being tested it a lot yet, seems to be a great project.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hello, @participant6. I couldn't make use of Trino directly to do it.

The main problem is that Trino does not passes to Iceberg the "initialize tables" option - which will do it "automagically" for you if the tables aren't present yet.

I would recommend you to initialize the tables yourself somehow before connecting to your metastore with Trino. I just can't give you more advice on it because I've given up this stack after knowing its limitations.

Good luck! Best regards!
